title: Prince and Princess of Wales in India ahead of meeting with Modi

 6 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Daniela Relph Senior royal correspondent, Mumbai Watch: Prince and Princess of Wales play street cricket in Mumbai The Prince and Princess of Wales have arrived in India for a three-day visit that will include a meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 The visit is the first time William and Catherine have been on an official overseas trip together in four years.
 Her cancer treatment has limited the amount of international travel she has undertaken but she will be with her husband for several engagements this week. 
 Most are related to the Earthshot Prize, founded by Prince William, which awards five £1m prizes for the best solutions to the biggest climate challenges.
 "The princess is enormously proud of what the prince has achieved with Earthshot and is really looking forward to being alongside him for what is one of the most important moments in his year," said a spokesperson for the royals. 
 "She's seen it develop into something truly remarkable and is excited to experience first-hand just how far it has come."
 Getty Images Catherine and William watched on as a game of cricket was played in a business district in Mumbai The couple's first engagement of their India visit was alongside a local cricketing superstar, Sachin Tendulkar.
 The cricketer was born and brought up in Mumbai and still holds the record for being the highest run scorer in international cricket. He is also a supporter of William's environmental Earthshot Prize.
 "I am very appreciative that the Royal Family has taken up such a noble cause," he told reporters.
 "The whole world is on this journey where we can positively make some changes to the planet, facing so many challenges, and make it a better place for the generations to follow."
 Tendulkar led William and Catherine in a game of street, or "gully", cricket in the Ballard Estate area of Mumbai.
 Press Association Press Association Both the prince and princess went into bat - sometimes facing one another - in a show of royal sporting rivalry.
 The royal couple were welcomed with a serving of chai tea under a large banyan tree in this picturesque part of the city which had a security cordon built around it for the royal visitors.
 Schoolchildren taking part in the event were unaware who their VIP guests were until minutes before they arrived.
 Press Association The royal couple also took a trip on the Mumbai Metro during their visit The royal couple's planned meeting with Modi on Wednesday was a late addition to the royal schedule.
 It came after the Indian prime minister confirmed he would be back from a scheduled trip to the Philippines in time to see the royals. 
 "For the Prince, it represents another significant engagement as he continues to take on a growing role on the international stage," a Kensington Palace spokesperson said.
 "We've seen him increasingly support the UK's diplomatic relationships through his overseas engagements, and this meeting will provide an opportunity to build on those connections at the highest level."
 The couple last met Modi on their official visit to India in 2016.
 Getty Images The royal couple met Modi 10 years ago during a seven-day tour of India and Bhutan Arriving in Mumbai earlier on Monday, Prince William posted a message about the trip on social media: "India has made an extraordinary contribution to Earthshot over the past six years and is home to more Earthshot finalists and winners than any other country."
 The royals will carry out a number of other engagements in Mumbai related to the environment, young families and the Bollywood film industry.
 At an Earthshot Prize Awards ceremony, five innovations will be announced as winners of the million-pound prizes. 
 Nominees range from projects to increase the number of electric rickshaws in India to a scheme able to detect wildfires faster than Nasa.
 The event will be hosted by Karan Johar, presenter of The Traitors India and one of the country's most well-known film makers.
 Take That will perform and guests will include actor Rami Malek and Australian conservationist and TV presenter Robert Irwin, who joined Prince William when he was a surprise guest on The Graham Norton show last month .
 "There is a lot of environmental potential here in Mumbai," said Irwin. "There is also a huge amount of young people who have a passion for environmentalism and I think Earthshot is mobilising that here in India."
